output.answer: As of November 2026, DoorDash is a defendant in Uber's antitrust lawsuit, which Uber filed in California Superior Court in San Francisco in February 2025 accusing DoorDash of coercing restaurants into exclusivity; the case remains active, with a California appellate panel hearing arguments on November 9, 2026 in DoorDash's appeal of a ruling keeping Uber's tortious-interference case in court rather than sending it to arbitration. DoorDash also remains a party to putative class actions, PAGA representative actions and individual arbitrations from Dashers challenging their classification as independent contractors, per its fiscal 2025 Form 10-K (the related San Francisco District Attorney misclassification suit was resolved in September 2025 for $2 million, and DoorDash is under a California EDD payroll-tax audit over the same classification issue). Consumers have separately sued over DashPass subscriptions (Divney v. DoorDash, filed July 10, 2025 in S.D.N.Y. alongside Apple Payments), and a consolidated data-breach suit, In re DoorDash, Inc. Data Breach Litigation, was pending in N.D. Cal. (3:25-cv-09926). DoorDash also agreed on September 28, 2026 to a record $131.5 million settlement with New York City over allegations it underpaid delivery workers and made late payments — news that triggered a securities-fraud investigation (no complaint filed yet) by a plaintiffs' firm after the stock fell 7.7%.
caveats: The $131.5 million New York City settlement is sourced to a plaintiffs' securities-law firm page; DoorDash's or NYC's own release was not in the corpus, and the terms/status (preliminary approval, payment mechanics) could not be independently verified.
The securities-fraud matter is only an investigation by a plaintiffs' firm with no complaint filed; no securities class action against DoorDash has been confirmed.

The In re DoorDash Data Breach docket shows a related civil case terminated by voluntary dismissal on April 8, 2026; the exact current posture of the consolidated data-breach litigation was not fully verifiable from the docket excerpt.

The DoorDash 10-K describes litigation generally and does not enumerate every pending case; the full universe of pending suits (including routine individual arbitrations and November 2026 filings) is incomplete.

output.question: What lawsuits is DoorDash involved in?

key_facts.fact: Uber sued DoorDash on Feb 14, 2025 in California Superior Court in San Francisco, accusing DoorDash of coercing restaurants into using DoorDash as their exclusive or sole preferred delivery provider and of anticompetitive practices

The Uber-DoorDash antitrust case is still active: on Nov 9, 2026 a three-judge California appellate panel heard arguments in DoorDash's appeal of a ruling favoring Uber that allowed Uber's tortious-interference case to stay in court rather than go to arbitration

DoorDash's FY2025 10-K discloses it is currently involved in putative class actions, PAGA representative actions, individual arbitration and court claims challenging classification of Dashers as independent contractors

The San Francisco District Attorney's June 2020 suit alleging DoorDash misclassified California Dashers as independent contractors was resolved in September 2025 for $2 million (a $2,102,000 final stipulated judgment signed Sept 11, 2025) with no injunctive relief

DoorDash is under audit by the California Employment Development Department for payroll-tax liabilities tied to classifying Dashers as independent contractors; a January 2023 assessment is being appealed and DoorDash has recorded an accrual as of Dec 31, 2025

Divney v. DoorDash, Inc. et al. (S.D.N.Y. 1:25-cv-05708, filed July 10, 2025) is a class action against DoorDash and Apple Payments Services alleging unauthorized DashPass subscription charges via the Caviar app with a deliberately complicated cancellation process

In re DoorDash, Inc. Data Breach Litigation (N.D. Cal., 3:25-cv-09926, Judge Araceli Martinez-Olguin) consolidated data-breach claims against DoorDash; docket last updated Oct 12, 2026, with a related civil case terminated on voluntary dismissal April 8, 2026

On September 28, 2026, DoorDash agreed to a record $131.5 million settlement with New York City over allegations it underpaid delivery workers and made late payments; DASH stock fell more than 7.7% that day
Law firm Bronstein, Gewirtz & Grossman is investigating potential securities-fraud claims against DoorDash over the NYC settlement news; as of the page's date no complaint had been filed

Docket aggregators show new suits still being filed against DoorDash in November 2026, including Muller v. DoorDash (S.D. Fla. 1:26-cv-27941, filed 11/09/2026) and a remand motion in Gabaldon v. DoorDash (E.D. Tenn. 3:26-cv-00397)
